sitefooterVocalSystemsForPeopleWhoWantTo: Vocal systems for people who want to be heard.
sitefooterTheSampleTakeIsReadByASyntheti: The sample take is read by a synthetic voice, and its review was written by hand in the format MicMane returns. Reviews of your own takes are AI feedback: check them against your recording before you rely on them.
sitenavUnlockTheFullPotentialOfYourVoice: Unlock the full potential of your voice.
sampleAClearStoryWithAStrongMiddleThe: A clear story with a strong middle. The pause and the slow “It's saying no” do real work. The opening rushes, and the ending fades on the very words “out loud”.
sampleSlowTheFirstLineDownAndHoldThe: Slow the first line down, and hold the last one up.
sampleRushedSetupWellJudgedSlowdownOnThe: Rushed setup, well-judged slowdown on the key line.
sampleMostlyLevelOneContrastCouldLift: Mostly level; one contrast could lift.
sampleEvenAndNeutralThroughoutMayBeAChoi: Even and neutral throughout; may be a choice.
sampleOneWellPlacedSilenceCarriesTheTurn: One well-placed silence carries the turn.
sampleTheOpeningLineRunsAtOneFastPace: The opening line runs at one fast pace, about 5.4 syllables a second. “Night shift” and “clinic downtown” get no more time than the words around them.
sampleThisLineSetsTheSceneAtThisSpeed: This line sets the scene. At this speed the listener catches the facts but has no time to picture them.
sampleSayTheFirstLineAgainAndGiveNight: Say the first line again and give “night shift” a beat longer than anything else in it.
sampleYouStopForAboutASecondAfterNobody: You stop for about a second after “nobody tells you”.
sampleTheGapMakesTheListenerLeanInThe: The gap makes the listener lean in. The point lands harder because they had to wait for it.
sampleKeepThisPauseToTestItTryIt: Keep this pause. To test it, try it half as long and listen for what you lose.
sampleTheHardestPartIsnTTheWorkStays: “The hardest part isn't the work” stays close to one pitch. The contrast between “hardest part” and “the work” isn't carried by the melody.
sampleTheSentenceSetsTwoThingsAgainstEac: The sentence sets two things against each other, and pitch movement can tell the listener which one matters. Other readings could work too.
sampleTryLiftingOnHardestAndLettingWorkF: Try lifting on “hardest” and letting “work” fall away.
sampleItSSayingNoSlowsRightDownWell: “It's saying no” slows right down, well below the rest of the take.
sampleThisIsThePointOfTheStoryAnd: This is the point of the story, and it gets the most time. The slowdown tells the listener to take it seriously.
sampleKeepTheSlowdownAndLeaveTheSilenceA: Keep the slowdown, and leave the silence after it just as long.
sampleTheLineSoundsEvenAndNeutralInThe: The line sounds even and neutral, in the same tone as the setup before it.
sampleTheWordsDescribeSomethingHardToDoA: The words describe something hard to do. A shift here, firmer or quieter and more personal, could carry that. A neutral reading can also work if you want restraint.
sampleRecordTheLineTwiceOnceFirmOnceAlmo: Record the line twice: once firm, once almost confiding. Keep the one that sounds like you mean it.
sampleTheLevelDropsSharplyOnOutLoudAnd: The level drops sharply on “out loud, and mean it”, the last words of the take.
sampleTheEndingIsThePromiseOfTheTalk: The ending is the promise of the talk, and it is the hardest part to hear. The drop also works against the words themselves.
sampleKeepOutLoudAndMeanItAtThe: Keep “out loud, and mean it” at the level of “So tonight”. Push breath through the last word rather than starting louder.
landingLearnWhatMakesAVoiceCarryPractise: Learn what makes a voice carry, practise out loud with a coach that listens, and grow more confident one take at a time.
landingTheCourseFollowsFiveFoundationsIn: The course follows five foundations, in order. Each lesson is one page: the lesson at the top, then every take you record under it, with its notes, so you can scroll back and hear what changed.
landingEachStripIsTheSameSampleTakeRead: Each strip is the same sample take, read through one foundation.
landingTheEndingDropsAwayOnOutLoudAnd: The ending drops away on “out loud, and mean it”.
landingTheEndingHoldsAtTheLevelOfSo: The ending holds at the level of “So tonight”.
landingAReviewOnlyMattersIfTheNextTake: A review only matters if the next take is better. Every note ends with something to try, and MicMane listens again.
landingTheVolumeLessonPageWithTwoTakesOf: The Volume lesson page, with two takes of the same line
landingSoTonightIWantToTalkAbout: So tonight, I want to talk about…
landingTakeOneIsTheSampleSMeasuredLevel: Take one is the sample's measured level. Take two is drawn to show the same line with the note followed.
landingTonalityDescribesHowYouSoundItNev: Tonality describes how you sound. It never guesses at your emotions, your confidence or your personality.
landingThereIsNoNumberForYourVoiceYou: There is no number for your voice. You get notes on moments, and a next take.
landingADeliveryThatAlreadyWorksIsLeftAl: A delivery that already works is left alone. “No clear problem” is a real answer.
landingTheSameSentenceCanLandInMoreThan: The same sentence can land in more than one way. When a note is a judgment call, it is marked tentative.
landingWhatItWillNeverTellYou: What it will never tell you.
landingHearingYourOwnVoiceIsExposingTheC: Hearing your own voice is exposing. The coach is built to describe what it hears, and to stop there.
landingThirtySecondsToAMinuteOnYourPhone: Thirty seconds to a minute, on your phone or laptop. The free review listens for all five foundations and pins its notes to your own words.
landingThirtySecondsIsEnoughToStart: Thirty seconds is enough to start.
